A red lamp on the right-hand pole seems to face the driver. If it is a working signal, the yield sign does not decide the order.
The key holds only if the truck has stopped (brake lights on): passing a moving truck by leaving the lane is overtaking, banned at intersections by point 77.1.
Key holds only if the white car counts as starting from a stop (point 36); if both count as simultaneous lane changers, point 39 makes the LEFT car (yellow) yield, the opposite of the key.

Key says press the upper part of the nose; NHS says pinch just above the nostrils, leaning forward, for 10-15 minutes.
Direct pressure is a wrong option in the key, but MedlinePlus advises it for an open fracture if bleeding continues.
Key includes pressing an artery pressure point; IFRC 2025 says first aiders should not use pressure points.
Key gives 60-80 bpm; MedlinePlus gives 60-100 bpm for resting adults, so the 80-100 option is also partly normal.
Key gives 12-18 breaths per minute; MedlinePlus gives 12-20 for resting adults.
Key adds a cold compress for suspected internal abdominal bleeding; IFRC says lie down, keep warm, call EMS and does not mention cold.
Key says remove a fallen wire with an insulating object; MedlinePlus forbids rescue near live high-voltage lines and coming within 6 m until power is off. Safety-critical.
Key says help only with sterile gloves; IFRC accepts any gloves or hands covered with plastic bags or cloth.
No page on the trusted sites states the adult leg-and-head injury pattern for a low car; text says so and gives only the IFRC spinal caution.
No page on the trusted sites states the child pelvis-and-chest injury pattern for a low car; text says so and gives only the IFRC spinal caution.
Key says lay the person on the back on a hard flat surface; IFRC says leave them as found and keep them still.

Key puts an unconscious head-injury casualty in the recovery position; MedlinePlus treats them as a spinal injury, rolls them only for vomiting, and says not to press directly on a wound if a skull fracture is suspected.
Key sets tourniquet limits of 1 hour warm and 30 minutes cold; WHO gives no such limit, says record the time and never loosen without a clinician.
Key bans all medicines; IFRC allows helping with the person's own medicine and suggesting aspirin for a suspected heart attack.
Key adds applying cold after covering the burn; IFRC warns against ice. Giving water is not covered by the pages checked.

review_findings.issue: The motorcycle has its left indicator on (crop: glow on its left side), so it is turning into the same road as you. The explanation says your paths do not meet and hides the real reason: a left-turning vehicle yields to an oncoming one going right (point 99, not cited).

The picture shows a traffic light on the far right corner with its red lamp lit and facing the driver. The explanation reasons only from sign 2.4 and never mentions it, although point 173 puts the light above priority signs. If the light is the driver's, the stated reason fails; needs a human look at the picture.

Says the reversing 'starts from the stop area'. In the picture the car stands past the yard entrance and the reversing arc starts there, well after the yellow 1.17 stop marking ends. The ban comes from point 50(6): the carriageway section that has a stop.

The bus has its right indicator on (crop), so it turns into the motorcycle's road and their paths do not cross. The explanation still says the bus yields to the motorcycle and never mentions the turn. By the logic of 5-24 and 5-65 (a right turn does not cross, so it does not wait; in 5-65 the key lets you go before a motorcycle on your right) the two could pass together; the options offer no such order, so the key rests only on a literal reading of point 98. Needs a human decision.

Says there is no pedestrian crossing here, but the picture shows a crossing sign (5.19) on the far side of the intersection (crop). The answer holds only because neither path reaches that crossing, which is the point the learner needs.

The picture shows the crossed-out city silhouette, which is 5.24.2. 5.24.1 is the version with the place name, matching the 5.23.1 (name) / 5.23.2 (silhouette) split that 4-131 uses. The meaning stays right, only the number is off.

Rule 86(4) bans parking closer than 50 m to a railway crossing, and 50 m is one of the options, so the official 25 m contradicts the law. The explanation says only that 25 m is not in the rules, never states the real 50 m, and tells the learner to memorize internal question numbers (7-6, 7-43, 7-68) that mean nothing to them.

Rule 86(4) bans parking closer than 50 m to a railway crossing, and 50 m is an offered option, so the official 15 m contradicts the law. The explanation says 15 m belongs to bus stops but never states the 50 m rule, so the learner is not told the real distance.

The picture marks 3 m from the curb to the line, and the motorcycle stands at the curb, so less than 3 m remains to the solid line. Rule 84(3) bans stopping there and 86(1) therefore bans parking, so the motorcycle also violates. Item 7-96 teaches exactly this for a motorcycle in the same 3 m layout. The explanation hides the conflict behind 'the official answer does not count it'.

The explanation defends 'do not touch and wait'. The cited CDC page says the opposite for a generalized seizure: turn the person gently onto one side, put something soft under the head, time the seizure and call for help if it lasts over 5 minutes. Only holding them down and putting things in the mouth are forbidden. A learner would leave a convulsing person on their back with an unprotected head.

The rule 'move the victim only when there is danger' also fits the rejected option, a power line on the car, which is plainly a danger. A learner would conclude they should pull the victim out. MedlinePlus 000053 says to stay 6 m away from live high-voltage contact, and that people in a vehicle struck by a power line stay inside unless there is a fire (the app's own 10-35).

'If a spinal injury is suspected, leave them in the same position' drops two conditions from the cited MedlinePlus 000022: only 'as long as breathing continues', and if the person vomits, roll the whole body to the side as one unit. Without them a learner may leave a vomiting unconscious person on their back.

The cited IFRC 2025 guideline does not say to seat the person, and gives no 'healthy lung works better' reason. It says to help them lie down in a comfortable position, for a chest injury possibly 'lying semi-propped up on their affected side'. The explanation presents the exam wording as if the source said it.

common_sense_findings.scene: The straight-only sign stands on a portable tripod, the U-turn-place sign is permanent; the temporary sign wins under point 172, which the explanation never says.
Same picture as 1-6: the portable straight-only sign overrides the permanent U-turn sign (point 172), and the yard is on the left, so the right-turn exception does not help.

U-turn around the median at a crossroad: A crosses the crossroad's centre line and runs on its correct half; B hugs the median nose on the near half, which is the oncoming side of the crossroad. The explanation says nothing forbids B.

The end-of-one-way sign (5.6) shows your road is one-way up to this junction, so the lane left of the broken line is not oncoming. That is why B, which looks like driving into the oncoming lane, is the correct path.

The red van shows its rear and tail lights to the junction, so as drawn it is driving away and takes no part in the order; the explanation never mentions it although it is a wrong option. Image check advised: if the van was meant to approach with a left indicator it would go last, so the answer holds either way.

PICTURE DEFECT. The officer is drawn from behind with both arms out, and the signal for arms out can only allow two OPPOSITE approaches (point 16(2)). The official answer allows two ADJACENT ones (blue/red and green) and only fits right arm forward at green (point 16(3)). Tried both body orientations; arms-out cannot give this answer, and the distractor (red banned) is exactly what arms-out would give. No older copy in data/old_pool. Fix the image: left arm down, right arm with baton pointing at the green car.

PICTURE DEFECT, same as 6-8. Officer from behind with both arms out, but the official answer (red and green may turn right) needs right arm forward at green: red on his left side, green at his chest (point 16(3)). With arms out, adjacent approaches cannot both move. Fix the image: left arm down, right arm with baton pointing at the green car.

The railed pit is in the truck's own lane, so by the usual rule (point 46) the truck would yield. The answer is the opposite only because signs 2.7 and 2.6 override that. The explanation never mentions the pit, which is the whole trap.

A red lamp on the right-hand pole appears to face the driver. If it is a working signal, sign 2.4 does not decide the order and the driver must wait, which the explanation ignores. If it is a leftover from the source photo, the official answer and the explanation both stand. Cropped and enlarged, but the picture cannot settle it; the owner should check it or clean the lamp from the image.

T-junction with a side road only on the right; the left side is just a gravel shoulder. Path C crosses the center line and bends back toward us on the oncoming side, so it is a U-turn, not the left turn the explanation calls it. Sign 4.1.4 has no left arrow, so it does not permit a U-turn.

Barrier in the lane with a 4.2.3 sign on it. Path B crosses the solid center line, which is what a learner would doubt. It is allowed because a temporary sign on a movable stand overrides the marking (point 174).

T-junction with sign 2.4 and marking 1.13; our car signals left; a grey car on the far lane comes from the right, at the junction mouth. Official 'No' contradicts the question's own condition (entry that does not hinder that car). Tried: center line is broken across the mouth, no sign bans the left turn, no stop line or 2.5 sign, point 1.13 text only requires stopping if necessary. The only scene argument is that the grey car is so close that any left turn would hinder it, but the question assumes it would not. Possibly a source key error or a picture swapped from a stop-line version.

Country road with only a broken center line (1.5) and faint edges. The official answer (bans driving left of the line or over it) describes a solid line 1.1, which is not in the picture. Enlarged the road and found no solid line; the repo has no original of this image to compare. Likely the picture lost or never had the solid line, so the picture needs checking against the source.
